newsitem.title: GERMANY: Top Germans do not trust ads as information-survey.
newsitem.headline: Top Germans do not trust ads as information-survey.

text.p: German leaders in politics, the media, industry and associations put little faith in advertising as a source of information, a industry survey showed on Tuesday.

Among those surveyed by German public relations agency Kohtes and Klewes and German Emnid research institute, 71 percent said they receive direct-marketing materials from companies, but only 12 percent use them to inform themselves.
The 29 percent without access to such advertising materials said they did not miss them.

The survey was conducted in April among 61 German parliamentarians, 86 top government officials, 78 senior editors and 53 leading representatives from industry and associations. It is carried out three times a year.

Ninety-six percent of those polled said they sought information in newspapers, 79 percent in magazines and 75 percent in trade publications. Sixty-eight percent said they watched television for information purposes.

A majority of business executives called daily newspapers their most important source of information, and most media representatives considered newspapers their most essential resource on the economy.
Participants regarded communication with people in their field as particularly useful, although the quality of the source was carefully considered.

Industry reports were named as a key source of information by 47 percent of all those polled and between 15 and 18 percent said they used the Internet, electronic mail and online services as research tools.
